TECH 3498 / ASSIGNMENT 6

Untrusted input. Measured evidence.

Cross-site scripting controls and a reproducible phishing-detection research experiment.

XSS LabSecurity ImprovementsResearch MethodMeasured ResultsSubmission & Evidence

Keep data out of the HTML parser.

Input validation constrains what your application accepts. A safe text sink keeps accepted input from becoming executable markup. These are complementary controls.

Try untrusted text

Not rendered yet.

This field is rendered as plain text only. Nothing is opened, fetched or executed. It is not saved. Character limits are validation, not an XSS filter.

Safe output with textContent

Encoded source for an HTML text context
The encoded source is shown as text. HTML-text encoding is not a universal encoder for URLs, JavaScript, CSS or arbitrary attribute contexts. Do not double-encode data before assigning textContent.

    
Why innerHTML changes the meaning
A fixed, harmless sample demonstrates HTML parsing. The markup in this frame is a trusted constant, never the text entered above. Scripts, network resources and origin access are blocked.
<strong>Lab marker</strong>
For user comments, plain text is the default. If a product genuinely needs rich HTML, use a maintained allowlist sanitizer and test its supported contexts. This lab does not implement a homemade HTML sanitizer.

  

  
SECURITY PROBLEM → CONTROL → MITIGATION → IMPROVEMENT
Document the trust boundary.

    
Security problemSecurity controlMitigationSecurity improvement / evidence

      
Typed markup reaches the local AI demo through innerHTML.Replace that display sink with textContent.HTML event-handler text stays inert, independent of prompt-guard setting.Regression tests verify literal payload text, no injected elements and no marker execution.

      
Oversized or malformed comments and URLs.Bound lengths and validate expected formats on the relevant input boundary.Reject invalid types/formats before processing. Validation does not replace output handling.This lab checks 1–2,000 characters; FastAPI validates HTTP(S) URL inputs separately.

      
Untrusted messages, announcements or model output become markup.Use DOM text APIs and framework text widgets.Keep user-generated content in text contexts.New lab output and existing A4 announcement/chat are checked with markup-shaped input.

      
Rich external content mixes with the application origin.Isolate the fixed demonstration with sandbox and restrictive CSP.No scripts, remote resources or same-origin access in the sample.Frame uses fixed trusted content. CSP is defense in depth, not a substitute for safe sinks.

    
Scope: this is a targeted fix and lab, not a claim that the entire site is production-secure. SentrySim retains its intentionally vulnerable XSS exercise for comparison. XSS and LLM prompt injection are distinct problems; a prompt guard is not a browser XSS defense.

  

  
PHISHGUARD / METHOD SELECTION
Can character patterns improve the lexical baseline?
Problem, question and objective
The existing lexical classifier detects phishing, but generates many false alarms. Aggregate URL counts lose the order of characters and short spelling patterns.
Question: Does combining a lexical Random Forest with a character-pattern classifier improve phishing F1 and false-positive rate?
Objective: compare phishing F1, precision, recall, false-positive/negative rates, average precision and ROC-AUC under the same domain-separated evaluation conditions.
Dataset: Malicious URLs dataset, Kaggle ↗
Version 1 · CC0 in the verified source metadata · benign and phishing subset.
Research results not loaded.

    
Hybrid feature/model approach
Baseline: existing lexical Logistic Regression, with Random Forest as the stronger comparator.
Proposed improvement: combine Random Forest probabilities from 19 numeric features with a linear classifier trained on hashed character 3–4-grams. Character order supplies a different representation of the same URL.
Validation: choose the mixture weight on an inner domain-separated validation partition. Keep threshold 0.5. Refit the character model on the outer training set, then compare all components on the same stored test rows.
This is an ensemble of traditional ML components using text and tabular representations. It does not claim deep learning, a connected LLM or novel state-of-the-art performance. An LLM is unnecessary for these URL classification experiments.

    
Fair comparison, ablations and computing requirements
Awaiting the experiment output.
Hashing has no learned vocabulary; the classifier is fitted only on training rows. Numeric imputation is fitted on training rows. URL validation, canonical duplicate/conflict removal and registrable-domain grouping follow the original raw-URL experiment.
Compare lexical-only, character-only and combined predictions. Select weight from 0.25, 0.50 and 0.75 using inner-validation F1, never test F1. A domain-cluster bootstrap summarizes uncertainty conditional on the fitted models.
The historical test set was already inspected in earlier project work. These results are exploratory. Independent temporal or external data is needed before making a confirmatory generalization claim.

  

  
ACTUAL PREDICTIONS / SAME HELD-OUT ROWS
Measure gains and trade-offs.
Awaiting measured results. No example metrics are substituted.
MethodAccuracyPrecisionRecallF1FPRFNRAPROC-AUC

    
Phishing F1 comparison
Higher F1 is better, but it does not capture every operational cost. Read the error rates and counts too.
Findings and limits
Awaiting results.
Average precision (AP) summarizes the precision–recall curve. It is not trapezoidal PR-AUC. Model probabilities are uncalibrated.

    
Confusion matrices and validation decisions

  

  
Evidence for review and submission.
Not run.
The controls test this lab’s rendering path and the corrected local AI display. They do not execute an arbitrary script in the workbench.
Reproduce the research
cd phishguard-ai
.venv\Scripts\python.exe assignment6\experiment.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe assignment6\verify_experiment.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe assignment6\make_deliverables.py
Training needs the existing downloaded dataset and saved trusted baseline artifacts. CPU only; no API key or paid service. Files live in phishguard-ai/assignment6. The deployed Flutter scanner continues using its existing baseline models.

    
References and remaining limitations
OWASP XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet · HashingVectorizer · SGDClassifier
Historical collection bias, unknown campaign overlap, hashing collisions, uncalibrated scores and single-split model selection limit inference. The bootstrap excludes training and model-selection variation. Review the generated write-up before submitting through Canvas.
